decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts extend the firm's core glass-processing and drilling know-how, so its in-house R&D can interpret results and refine the product.
Carrier wafers for small-diameter handling sit squarely within the firm's established carrier offer and its strategic push toward reusable carriers.
The Cu-interposer glass wafer builds on existing glass-wafer structuring and metallization capability and fits the firm's direction toward multifunctional packaging wafers.
The off-the-shelf brand reuses the firm's standard glass and quartz wafer competence and needs little new knowledge, though as a sales channel it could be folded back into the main brand.
Glass-based circuit boards lie far from the firm's wafer-centric knowledge base, making early results hard to assimilate, so resources are better redirected to core substrate development.
